metadata.case_name: LAU KWAI KWONG v. YIU WING CONSTRUCTION CO LTD AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_after: toll-collector, security guard or a worker in a gas filing station
plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: toll-collector, security guard or a worker in a gas filing station

injuries.description: Fracture of the right distal radius (fixed with open reduction and plating).
source: he suffered an injury to his right distal radius when struck by a falling object on a building site.
The radius fracture was fixed with an open reduction and plating.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of lower end of radius

injuries.description: Dislocation of the distal radio-ulnar joint (transfixed with a metal wire).
source: The distal radio-ulnar joint was dislocated in the accident.
The dislocated distal radio-ulnar joint was transfixed with a metal wire and his forearm was put into a cast for mobilization.
injuries.icd_description: Dislocation or sprain of other specified joints or ligaments at wrist or hand level

injuries.description: Non-union of the ulnar styloid and the site of the fracture at the base of the ulnar styloid.
source: Radiologically there has been non-union of the ulnar styloid and the site of the fracture at the base of the ulnar styloid.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture at other specified part of wrist or hand level

manifestations.description: Significant pain in exertion such as lifting heavy objects and twisting activities
Weakness in exertion such as lifting heavy objects and twisting activities
Pain on resisted pronation of the wrist

treatments_received: The radius fracture was fixed with an open reduction and plating.
The dislocated distal radio-ulnar joint was transfixed with a metal wire
his forearm was put into a cast for mobilization.
he received a course of physiotherapy and later occupational therapy.
treatments_future: medical advisors have recommended further surgery to him which would cost about $40,000, but he has elected not to undertake that surgery.

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenity for which PSLA of $200,000 was awarded.
His total loss of earning capacity has been assessed at 8%.
